summary: The paper describes the CRAY-1 vector computer, including its registers, interleaved memory, chained functional units and cooling. It also explains how the optimizing Fortran compiler vectorizes innermost DO loops and reports timings for simple loops and library routines.
why_read: It is a readable primary account of a 1970s vector machine and the vectorizing compiler built for it, useful as a single-processor baseline.
main_contribution: A description of the CRAY-1 architecture and its vectorizing Fortran compiler, with loop timing data.
main_limitation: The paper reports that most early compiled Fortran loops ran slower than hand-coded machine code, and it covers one processor only.
evaluation_method: Cited independent benchmark studies plus vendor timings of simple DO loops and library routines, in clock periods per result.
benchmarks: Table III: 16 simple DO loops at N = 1 to 1000
Fig. 7: scalar and vector library routine timings
Independent matrix benchmark studies cited as refs 3 and 4
